messages:
Maya Patel: FYI  we have a P1 from Acme about intermittent 504s and API 5xx on hosted inference (/v1/generate). Support says it's spikey during 09:30-09:50 PST  lots of short requests, mostly short prompts, but lots of concurrent clients. They attached a few request IDs.

Raj Singh: @Maya thanks. Any common error body? 5xx code from gateway or model pods?

Maya Patel: Gateway 504s and some 502s. Support pasted a stack snippet: "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection failure". Also saw "context deadline exceeded" in logs. Support-bot forwarded request IDs: req-8a1, req-8a2, req-8b0.

Samir Chen: Sounds like scale-up lag -> requests hit gateway while pods are scheduling/warming. Can you grab k8s events for the model deployment and the KEDA ScaledObject?

Maya Patel: Attaching output from earlier (trimmed):
```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=model-acme -o wide
NAME                                  READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
model-acme-5b9d7c9c9d-7fjk2          0/1     ContainerCreating 0   2m
model-acme-5b9d7c9c9d-9xkq1          1/1     Running   0          15m
```

Maya Patel: KEDA ScaledObject shows triggers on deployment queue length (Prometheus rule):
```
triggers:
  - type: prometheus
    metadata:
      serverAddress: http://prometheus.monitoring.svc
      query: sum(rate(redis_queue_length[1m]))
      threshold: '5'
```

Tessa Lf3pez: Two immediate red flags: 1) new pods stuck ContainerCreating for ~2min -> maybe image pull or node pressure; 2) warmup time for that model binary is ~60-90s (loads weights into GPU). If KEDA scales pods up but they are not ready, gateway still routes? Gateway should only route to Ready endpoints, but we have observed connection resets  maybe kube-proxy or envoy connection attempts to pods while they're initializing (readiness probe not blocking) or load balancer retries.

Samir Chen: Check the readinessProbe config  I recall we've used an HTTP probe hitting /health which returns 200 even while weights are still loading (we added lightweight health check to speed up LB). If readiness returns 200 before model ready, traffic will land on pod and time out while init finishes.

Raj Singh: Show deploy spec & readiness/liveness sections.

Maya Patel: Here's relevant excerpt:
```
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10
  timeoutSeconds: 2
```

Maya Patel: And startup logs show:
```
[INFO] starting model server
[INFO] loading weights (this can take 75s)
[WARN] accepting traffic before kv-cache primed
[ERROR] request timeout after 30s
```

Tessa Lf3pez: There we go. Readiness is too permissive and initialDelaySeconds too low. Pod readiness should be false until weights loaded and kv-cache primed. Also KEDA's scaling may be reactive  it determines desired replicas, but the real throughput drop means backlog grew and gateway timed out clients while new pods were still booting.

infra-bot: @channel Incident: autoscale-backpressure - investigating. Links: https://console.redwood/prod/inference/alerts/1234

Samir Chen: Immediate mitigations:
- Increase readinessProbe to call /ready (endpoint that validates weights + kv primed) or add a startup probe to block traffic. Example:
```
startupProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /ready
    port: 8080
  failureThreshold: 30
  periodSeconds: 10
```
- Set KEDA minReplicaCount to a non-zero value for this SKU (e.g., 2) to keep warm capacity.
- Add a short-lived prewarm pool or keep-a-warm node group (dedicated warm instances) for spikes.

Raj Singh: For now, can we temporarily increase minReplicas on the ScaledObject to 2 and patch readiness to /ready? If image pull is long we should check node pool capacity.

Tessa Lf3pez: Also bump gateway timeout to 90s to give pods time to finish warmup when scaling (short term).

Maya Patel: I'm going to patch ScaledObject + deployment now.

Maya Patel: kubectl patch scaledobject model-acme --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":2}}' -n inference

Samir Chen: I pushed a small change to the model container: added /ready endpoint that blocks until kv_cache.ready == true and weights_loaded == true. Please redeploy.

Maya Patel: Redeploy done. Also bumped envoy route timeout to 90s for this host:PATCH applied.

Maya Patel: After patch metrics: new pods come up faster (image was fine). Model logs show weights loaded and /ready returns 200. Traffic acceptance aligns with readiness now. Errors decreased.

support-bot: Customer updated: "we're seeing far fewer 504s now, still occasional but much better" :thumbsup: 

Raj Singh: Follow-ups:
- Create a permanent prewarm config for this model (minReplicaCount=2 or dedicated pool).
- Add automated healthcheck for readiness endpoint in our model onboarding checklist.
- Update KEDA trigger to consider avg startup time: maybe scale proactively using predictive scaler or prewarm window.
- Evaluate making gateway fallback to smaller model (less warmup) during spikes.

Maya Patel: Action items assigned: Samir -> merge readiness /ready fixes across model images. Tessa -> update runbook and add prewarm option. Raj -> run an experiment with KEDA predicted scaling and telemetry to measure reduced 504s. Support -> issue credit to Acme per SLA and confirm resolution.

Samir Chen: Note for postmortem: root cause = permissive readiness probe + long model startup (weights + kv-cache) + reactive KEDA scale path. Secondary contributor: gateway timeout defaults too low (30s) causing client 504s.

Tessa Lf3pez: I'll draft postmortem. ETA 48h.

Maya Patel: Closing timeline: first alert 1876543210, mitigations applied by 1876544300, errors down by 1876545000. Will attach graphs and request traces to the PM.

infra-bot: Incident marked resolved (oncall: Raj Singh).

Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups scheduled in #eng-ml-runbooks.
